topics.title: Agent Architectures
topics.description: Agent architectures define how an AI agent is structured: how it reasons, selects tools, manages memory, and decides when to stop. Common patterns include ReAct (reason + act), plan-and-execute, and tree-of-thought. Choosing the right architecture depends on how much control the application needs over model behavior and how tolerant the customer is of unpredictable agent outputs.

topics.title: AI Agents
topics.description: AI agents are systems where a language model is given tools and a goal, and takes a sequence of actions to complete a task rather than responding to a single prompt. Agents can call APIs, search the web, write and run code, and read files. In practice, most well-designed agents use one LLM call as an orchestrating layer with a series of tool calls around it. The guiding principle is to start with the smallest unit of autonomy, prove it works, and only then expand what the agent is allowed to do.
resources: What are AI Agents? - Agents in Artificial Intelligence Explained
AI Agents Explained in Simple Terms for Beginners

topics.title: AI Engineering Skills
topics.description: AI engineering involves building software systems that use machine learning models and large language models (LLMs) as components. This includes selecting models, integrating them via APIs, engineering prompts, managing context, and deploying AI features in production. AI engineering is at the core of the job of FDEs. It's what turns an AI model into a product that runs reliably inside a company's infrastructure.
resources: What Is an AI Engineer? (And How to Become One)
A Practical Guide To Becoming An AI Engineer (2026)
AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Generative AI Explained
AI Engineering Vs AI Forward Deployed Engineer(FDE)

topics.title: AI Governance
topics.description: AI governance refers to the policies, processes, and controls that ensure AI systems behave safely, fairly, and in compliance with regulations and organizational standards. This includes defining acceptable use, managing model risk, ensuring transparency in AI decision-making, and monitoring for bias or harmful outputs.
resources: AI Governance Best Practices: How to Build Responsible and Effective AI Programs
Security & AI Governance: Reducing Risks in AI Systems

topics.title: Airflow
topics.description: Apache Airflow is an open-source workflow orchestration platform for scheduling and monitoring data pipelines. Pipelines are defined as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) in Python, where each node represents a task. Airflow provides a web interface for monitoring runs, managing dependencies, and handling retries and alerts.
resources: Building Pipelines In Apache Airflow – For Beginners

topics.title: API Security
topics.description: API security covers the practices and controls needed to protect APIs from unauthorized access and abuse. This includes authentication, authorization, rate limiting, input validation, and protection against common attacks like injection and replay attacks. Poorly secured APIs are a common attack vector in production systems.

topics.title: APIs Design
topics.description: API design is the process of defining how services communicate with each other through well-structured interfaces. Good API design involves choosing the right protocol (REST, GraphQL, gRPC), defining clear resource models, handling errors consistently, and versioning carefully. A well-designed API is predictable, easy to use, and stable over time.
resources: APIs for Beginners - How to use an API (Full Course / Tutorial)

topics.title: Authentication
topics.description: Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user or system. Common mechanisms include username/password, API keys, OAuth 2.0 tokens, and JWTs. Authentication is distinct from authorization, which governs what an authenticated user is allowed to do. Getting authentication right is foundational to securing any application that handles user data or sensitive operations.

topics.title: AWS
topics.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the largest cloud platform by market share, offering hundreds of services including compute (EC2, Lambda), storage (S3), databases (RDS, DynamoDB), networking, and AI/ML tooling. It has a deep ecosystem of third-party integrations and is the most widely used cloud platform across startups and enterprises.
resources: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner Training 2020 - Full Course

topics.title: Azure
topics.description: Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform with particularly strong adoption in enterprise environments, especially those using Active Directory, Office 365, and .NET. It offers compute, storage, networking, databases, DevOps tooling, and AI services including Azure OpenAI Service.

topics.title: Backend
topics.description: Backend development refers to the server-side logic of a web application, including handling requests, running business logic, interacting with databases, and returning responses. Backend systems are typically built with Python, Node.js, Java, or Go, connected to databases and external services. FDEs who can build solid backend systems can own the full delivery of a feature rather than handing off at the API boundary.
resources: What is backend? A comprehensive intro to server-side development

topics.title: Building Eval Pipelines
topics.description: Evaluation pipelines are automated systems for measuring the quality of an AI model or application over a set of test cases. A good eval does not just check whether the final answer is correct. It traces the steps a skilled human would take to solve the same problem and grades the agent on each one. Building this starts with a golden dataset: a set of real queries with the ideal output labeled by hand. That becomes the standard everything else is measured against.

topics.title: Business Acumen
topics.description: Business acumen is the ability to understand how an organization operates, what its priorities are, how it makes money, and where technology can create real value. Being able to connect engineering decisions to business outcomes is what makes FDEs different from traditional software engineers.
resources: Business acumen for FDEs: follow the money before you write the first line of code

topics.title: C++
topics.description: C++ is a high-performance, statically typed language that gives developers fine-grained control over memory and system resources. It is used in systems programming, game engines, embedded software, and performance-critical applications. It supports both procedural and object-oriented programming styles.
resources: C++ Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course

topics.title: Choosing your Model Provider
topics.description: Different LLM providers offer models with different tradeoffs in capability, cost, latency, context length, and licensing terms. Common providers include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta (open weights), and Mistral. Choosing the right model for a use case involves evaluating benchmarks, pricing, API reliability, data privacy terms, and whether the model's strengths match the application's requirements.
resources: How to Choose Large Language Models: A Developer’s Guide to LLMs
Choose the right AI model for your use case

topics.title: Claude Code
topics.description: Claude Code is an AI coding assistant built on Anthropic's Claude model. It can write, edit, explain, and debug code across a wide range of languages and frameworks, and is designed to handle complex multi-file tasks and refactoring alongside code generation.
resources: CLAUDE CODE FULL COURSE 4 HOURS: Build & Sell (2026)

topics.title: Cloud Platforms
topics.description: Cloud platforms provide on-demand access to computing resources including servers, storage, networking, databases, and managed services. Instead of running physical hardware, teams deploy and scale their applications on cloud infrastructure. The major providers each offer a broad set of services that cover most infrastructure needs.
resources: Cloud Computing In 6 Minutes | What Is Cloud Computing?

topics.title: Codex
topics.description: Codex is OpenAI's code-focused model, trained on large amounts of public code. It can generate code from natural language descriptions, complete functions, and help with documentation. It is the model that powers GitHub Copilot and one of the foundational tools that popularized AI-assisted coding as a mainstream workflow.

topics.title: Communication
topics.description: If you cannot explain what AI can and cannot do to a non-technical VP, you cannot be an FDE. Communication in this role is about translating between two different worlds: the technical reality of what you are building and the business reality of what the customer needs to justify the investment. That means being able to speak about token costs and latency in the same conversation where you are explaining ROI to an executive. It also means knowing when to say AI is not the right answer.
resources: 6 Strategies to Improve Your Communication Skills as a Software Developer
Beyond Code: Communication Skills Every Software Engineer Needs
Talk Like a Strategy Consultant (McKinsey's Culture)
TALK LIKE A CONSULTANT - Top down communication explained (management consulting skills)

topics.title: Containers
topics.description: Containers are a lightweight way to package an application along with its dependencies and configuration so it runs consistently across different environments. Unlike virtual machines, containers share the host operating system kernel, making them fast to start and efficient to run. Docker is the most common tool for building and running containers.

topics.title: Context Engineering
topics.description: Context engineering is the practice of strategically curating, structuring, and refining the information provided to a Large Language Model to ensure accurate and relevant outputs. It involves techniques like prompt crafting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and managing conversation memory to provide the model with the necessary background knowledge for specific tasks.
resources: Effective context engineering for AI agents
Context Engineering for AI Agents: A Deep Dive
Context engineering explained: What every AI developer should know

topics.title: CSS
topics.description: CSS, or Cascading Style Sheets, controls the visual appearance of HTML elements on a web page. It handles layout, colors, typography, spacing, animations, and responsive design. Modern CSS includes Flexbox, Grid, and custom properties that make it possible to build complex, adaptive layouts.
resources: CSS Tutorial – Full Course for Beginners

topics.title: Cursor
topics.description: Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built on top of VS Code that integrates LLMs directly into the coding experience. It supports chat-based code editing, multi-file edits, codebase-aware completions, and agent-style workflows where the model can make changes across an entire project.
resources: Cursor Tutorial for Beginners (AI Code Editor)

topics.title: Data Engineering
topics.description: Data engineering involves building and maintaining the systems that collect, store, process, and move data at scale. This includes designing pipelines, working with data warehouses, and ensuring data quality for downstream consumers like analysts and ML systems.

topics.title: Data Modeling
topics.description: Data modeling is the process of deciding how data should be structured and stored so it can be queried efficiently and understood by the people who use it. Common patterns include the star schema, where a central fact table is surrounded by dimension tables; the one big table (OBT) approach favored in some analytics workloads; and the medallion architecture used in data lakehouses, where data flows through bronze (raw), silver (cleaned), and gold (aggregated) layers.
resources: What is Data Modelling? Beginner's Guide to Data Models and Data Modelling

topics.title: Data Pipelines
topics.description: A data pipeline is a series of steps that move and transform data from one place to another, usually from source systems into a warehouse or processing layer. Pipelines can be batch-based (running on a schedule) or streaming (processing data as it arrives). Building reliable pipelines involves handling failures, schema changes, and data validation.
resources: What is a Data Pipeline? - IBM
Build a Data Engineering Pipeline using Python and Airflow
Building Data Pipelines with Apache Kafka and Confluent

topics.title: Data Privacy & Compliance
topics.description: Data privacy and compliance involves handling personal or sensitive data according to applicable laws and organizational policies. Relevant regulations include GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, and others depending on the industry and geography. For AI systems, this includes what data is sent to third-party model APIs, what is stored, and how long it is retained.
resources: Security, Compliance, and Data for Forward Deployed Engineers
Data Security: Protect your critical data (or else)

topics.title: Data Warehouses
topics.description: A data warehouse is a system optimized for analytical queries across large volumes of structured data. The major platforms in enterprise environments are Snowflake, Google BigQuery, and Amazon Redshift. Unlike operational databases, warehouses are designed for reading and aggregating data rather than frequent writes, and they typically sit at the center of a company's analytics and BI infrastructure.
resources: Database vs Data Warehouse vs Data Lake | What is the Difference?

topics.title: Day 2 Operations
topics.description: Day 2 Operations refers to everything that happens after a system goes live. Day 1 is the launch. Day 2 is the ongoing work of keeping the system running, monitoring for failures, handling edge cases that were not anticipated during development, and responding to feedback from real users.
resources: Day 2 Operations: A Practical Guide for Managing Post-Deployment Complexity

topics.title: Debugging Agent Logic
topics.description: Debugging AI agent logic involves tracing through the sequence of reasoning steps, tool calls, and decisions an agent made to find where it went wrong. This is harder than debugging traditional code because agent behavior is non-deterministic and depends on model outputs. Structured logging, step-by-step traces, and replay capabilities are the main tools for making agent failures visible and reproducible.
resources: How to Debug, Evaluate, and Ship Reliable AI Agents with LangSmith

topics.title: The Delta
topics.description: The Delta is the original term Palantir used for what is now called an FDE. It refers to the gap between what a software product does out of the box and what a specific customer actually needs. A Delta is both a role (the engineer who closes that gap) and a concept (the custom work required to make a product work in a real environment). In FDE interviews, you may be asked to identify the Delta in a given customer scenario, meaning the specific technical or workflow gap that needs to be bridged.
resources: A Comprehensive Analysis of Palantir’s Forward Deployed Engineering Model
How Palantir Invented the Forward Deployed Engineer Model and Why AI Startups Are Adopting It

topics.title: DevOps Skills
topics.description: DevOps is the practice of automating and streamlining how software is built, tested, and deployed. A forward-deployed engineer who knows DevOps can own the full deployment lifecycle, from spinning up infrastructure to shipping a containerized agent into a client's cloud environment, without depending on another team to get there.
resources: What Is DevOps? A Guide to the Basics

topics.title: DevSecOps
topics.description: DevSecOps integrates security practices directly into the DevOps pipeline rather than treating security as a final gate before release. This includes automated security scanning in CI/CD, dependency vulnerability checks, secrets management, and security review as part of the development process. The goal is to catch and fix security issues early and continuously rather than at the end.
resources: DevSecOps Course for Beginners – API Security

topics.title: Discovery & Scoping
topics.description: Discovery and scoping is the phase of a customer engagement where the team identifies the problem to solve, understands the current state of the customer's systems and processes, and defines what success looks like. It involves asking the right questions, identifying constraints, and setting realistic expectations before any building begins. Getting this phase right determines whether the rest of the engagement goes smoothly or runs into avoidable problems.
resources: AI Techniques (Production): Use Case Discovery & System Scoping

topics.title: Docker
topics.description: Docker is the leading platform for building, shipping, and running containers. A Dockerfile defines the steps to build a container image, and Docker provides tools to run those images locally or push them to a registry for deployment. It is the standard way to package applications for consistent behavior across development, staging, and production environments.
resources: Docker Crash Course for Absolute Beginners

topics.title: Data Structures & Algorithms
topics.description: Data structures are ways of organizing data in memory, such as arrays, linked lists, trees, graphs, and hash maps. Algorithms are step-by-step procedures for solving problems, like sorting, searching, or traversal. Knowing these well means being able to evaluate performance characteristics of code, debug inefficiencies in customer systems, and reason clearly about solutions to technical problems.
resources: Learn Data Structures and Algorithms Visually – Crash Course

topics.title: Embedded Engineering
topics.description: Embedded engineering describes the physical and organizational model of an FDE engagement: the engineer is embedded inside the customer's team, not working remotely or at arm's length. This means joining the customer's Slack, attending their standups, working in their codebase, and being present in the environment where the problems actually live.
resources: Forward Deployed AI Engineers: What They Are and When You Need One

topics.title: Enterprise Workflow
topics.description: Enterprise workflows are the processes and systems through which large organizations operate, including approvals, handoffs, integrations with existing tools, and compliance requirements. Building for enterprise environments requires understanding these workflows and designing solutions that fit within them.
resources: What Is Workflow Automation? A Guide for Enterprise

topics.title: Executive Reporting
topics.description: Executive reporting is the practice of communicating the status of a technical engagement to non-technical decision makers in a format they can act on. A good executive update leads with value delivered, not tasks completed. It flags risks clearly and pairs each one with a required action or decision. It connects technical milestones to business outcomes so the reader understands why the work matters, not just that it is happening.
resources: What Is Executive Reporting? (Definition and Best Practices)
Executive reporting: how to create better reports (+ free example)

topics.title: FDE Tiers
topics.description: Not all FDE roles are the same. The job market has split into three distinct tiers with different skill requirements. AI lab FDEs need deep ML fluency, strong agent architecture skills, and the ability to help customers adopt models in production. Enterprise software FDEs need data platform depth, integration experience, and the ability to connect a vendor's product to a customer's existing data infrastructure. Consulting and staffing FDEs need broad solutions architecture skills, account management instincts, and the ability to run an end-to-end engagement independently. Knowing which tier you are targeting shapes which parts of this roadmap to prioritize.
resources: How AI Labs Are Solving The Last Mile Problem
Forward Deployed roles: the emerging job family
AI Engineers, Applied Scientists, Forward Deployed Engineers: Let's Unpack.

topics.title: From X to FDE
topics.description: Three backgrounds tend to transition well into the FDE role: software engineers, consultants, and product managers. Software engineers already have the technical foundation but often need to develop the ability to communicate AI tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders and build a portfolio that shows they can own a full deployment, not just write code. Consultants and PMs can already translate data into business outcomes, which is half the job, but need to close the gap on engineering by building real agents, RAG pipelines, and eval frameworks from scratch.
resources: How to Become a Forward Deployed Engineer:
How to Transition from a Developer or Architect to AI FDE roles
The Definitive Guide to Forward Deployed Engineer Interviews in 2026

topics.title: Frontend
topics.description: Frontend development refers to the part of web development concerned with what users see and interact with in a browser. It covers HTML for structure, CSS for styling, and JavaScript for interactivity. FDEs who can build functional frontends are more self-sufficient in customer engagements, able to deliver end-to-end demos and working prototypes without depending on a separate frontend team.

topics.title: GCP
topics.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is Google's cloud offering, known for strong data and analytics services like BigQuery and AI/ML infrastructure like Vertex AI. It is often the preferred choice for data-intensive workloads and organizations already using Google Workspace.

topics.title: Gemini
topics.description: Gemini is Google DeepMind's family of multimodal AI models, capable of processing and generating text, code, images, and more. It is available via Google AI Studio and Vertex AI in different sizes with varying tradeoffs in speed and capability.
resources: How To Master Google Gemini in 2026 (Free Course)

topics.title: Git & GitHub
topics.description: Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes to code over time and allows multiple people to collaborate on the same codebase without overwriting each other's work. GitHub builds on top of Git with features like pull requests, code review, issue tracking, and CI/CD integrations. Both are standard tools in nearly every software development workflow today.

topics.title: Go
topics.description: Go is a statically typed, compiled language developed by Google, designed for simplicity and performance. It is commonly used for building backend services, command-line tools, and cloud infrastructure components. Its concurrency model, based on goroutines and channels, makes it well suited for network-heavy and distributed workloads.

topics.title: GraphQL
topics.description: GraphQL is a query language and runtime for APIs that lets clients request exactly the fields they need, rather than consuming fixed endpoints with predefined shapes. This reduces over-fetching, makes APIs more flexible, and is especially useful in frontend-heavy applications with complex or variable data requirements.

topics.title: HTML
topics.description: HTML, or HyperText Markup Language, is the standard language for structuring content on the web. It defines the elements of a page such as headings, paragraphs, links, forms, and images. It is the foundation that CSS and JavaScript build on top of.
resources: What is HTML – Definition and Meaning of Hypertext Markup Language
HTML Tutorial for Beginners: HTML Crash Course

topics.title: Inference Optimization
topics.description: Inference optimization refers to techniques for making model predictions faster and cheaper without significantly reducing quality. Common approaches include quantization (reducing numerical precision), distillation (training a smaller model to mimic a larger one), caching repeated requests, and batching. These optimizations are especially relevant for LLMs, where inference costs can be substantial at scale.
resources: How can I optimize for an inference application?
Mastering LLM Inference Optimization From Theory to Cost Effective Deployment:

topics.title: Integration Engineering
topics.description: Integration engineering is the practice of connecting systems that were not designed to work together. This usually means building APIs over existing data layers, bridging incompatible authentication systems, chaining tools across services with different data formats, and wrapping third-party products in interfaces a new system can use reliably. Most of the technical difficulty in real-world AI deployments lives here, not in the model itself.
resources: Software Integration: Examples and Why It’s Important

topics.title: Introduction
topics.description: A Forward Deployed Engineer is a software engineer who works directly inside a customer's environment to build, deploy, and stabilize AI systems. The role originated at Palantir, where engineers called Deltas would embed with clients, sometimes on military bases, to ship code overnight based on feedback from the field that same day. That same idea is now at the center of how companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are bringing AI into large enterprises. The job requires technical depth, the ability to read an unfamiliar codebase quickly, and the communication skills to explain what AI can and cannot do to a non-technical decision maker.
resources: Forward deployed engineer is AI’s hottest job
How to Become a Forward Deployed Engineer in 2026

topics.title: Java / Scala
topics.description: Java is a statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) and is widely used in enterprise systems, backend services, and Android development. Scala is also a JVM language that blends object-oriented and functional programming styles, commonly used in data processing with Apache Spark.
resources: Scala Crash Course by a Scala Veteran (with some JavaScript flavor)

topics.title: JavaScript / TypeScript
topics.description: JavaScript is the programming language of the web, running natively in browsers and on servers via Node.js. TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static type annotations, catching errors at compile time and improving code maintainability at scale. Together they are the dominant choice for full-stack web development.
resources: JavaScript Crash Course - Tutorial for Complete Beginners
Learn TypeScript – Crash Course for Beginners

topics.title: JavaScript
topics.description: JavaScript is the scripting language that runs in web browsers, giving web pages dynamic behavior. It handles user interactions, DOM manipulation, and API requests. On the server side, it runs via Node.js, making it possible to use a single language across the full web stack.
resources: JavaScript Tutorial Full Course - Beginner to Pro

topics.title: Kubernetes
topics.description: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system that automates the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. It handles scheduling containers across a cluster, managing service discovery, load balancing, rolling updates, and self-healing by restarting failed containers. It is the standard platform for running containers in production at scale.

topics.title: Last-Mile Integration
topics.description: Last-mile integration refers to the final set of connections between a product and the specific systems, data sources, and workflows of a customer environment. It is called last-mile because it is often the shortest but hardest part of a deployment: the product works in general, but making it work with this particular customer's setup requires custom engineering.
resources: What a forward deployed engineer does, and how to tell if you are ready
The Last Mile of AI: Why Forward Deployed Engineers Are Becoming the Most Critical Role in Enterprise AI Delivery
What is a Forward Deployed Engineer(FDE)? The "Last Mile" Special Ops of the AI Revolution

topics.title: Learn a Programming Language
topics.description: Learning a programming language involves mastering the syntax, semantics, and standard libraries of a specific tool used to instruct computers. This process begins by understanding fundamental programming constructs like variables, data types, control flow, and functions, and progresses to utilizing idiomatic patterns to write efficient and maintainable code.
resources: Best Programming Languages to Learn for an FDE Role
The Forward Deployed Engineer Tech Stack: Tools, Languages, and Frameworks
The Exact Tools, Languages and Frameworks Forward Deployed Engineers Rely On

topics.title: Linux
topics.description: Linux is an open-source operating system used widely in servers, cloud environments, and developer workstations. Most production software runs on Linux, so being comfortable navigating a Linux system, managing processes, reading logs, and configuring services is a practical necessity for anyone building and deploying in real customer environments.

topics.title: LLM Fundamentals
topics.description: Large language models (LLMs) are machine learning models trained on large amounts of text data that can generate, summarize, classify, and reason about language. They work by predicting the most likely next tokens given a context window of input. Understanding how LLMs work, including their limitations around hallucination, context length, and latency, is the foundation for building reliable systems around them.
resources: What is a large language model (LLM)?

topics.title: Managed ML Services
topics.description: Managed ML services are cloud provider offerings that abstract away the infrastructure for training, deploying, and serving machine learning models. Examples include AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI, and Azure Machine Learning. They handle provisioning, scaling, and monitoring so teams can focus on the model and data rather than the underlying infrastructure.

topics.title: MCP
topics.description: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources through a unified interface. Instead of building custom integrations for every tool, developers implement MCP servers that expose tools and resources in a standardized way. This makes it easier to compose agents that work with many different services.
resources: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
MCP Explained: How Modern AI Agents Connect to the Real World
What is MCP? Integrate AI Agents with Databases & APIs
How Model Context Protocol (MCP) actually works

topics.title: Memory & State Management
topics.description: Memory in AI agents refers to how information is stored and retrieved across steps in a conversation or task. Short-term memory lives in the context window, while long-term memory requires external storage like a database or vector store. Managing state well is important for agents that need to track progress, avoid repetition, and stay consistent over longer interactions.
resources: Storing and Retrieving Knowledge for Agents
Building Brain-Like Memory for AI Agents

topics.title: MLOps
topics.description: MLOps applies DevOps principles to machine learning systems, covering the processes and tooling needed to reliably build, deploy, monitor, and update ML models in production. This includes versioning data and models, automating training pipelines, serving inference at scale, and detecting model degradation over time.
resources: MLOps: What It Is, Why It Matters, and How to Implement It
MLOps Course – Build Machine Learning Production Grade Projects

topics.title: Multi-Agents
topics.description: Multi-agent systems involve multiple AI agents working together, where each agent has a specific role or capability and they coordinate to complete a larger task. One agent might plan the work while others execute specific subtasks, and a final agent synthesizes the results. This pattern improves reliability and modularity for complex workflows that would overwhelm a single agent.
resources: Multi Agent Systems Explained: How AI Agents & LLMs Work Together

topics.title: Node.js
topics.description: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that lets developers run JavaScript on the server side. It uses a non-blocking, event-driven architecture that makes it efficient for I/O-heavy workloads like APIs, real-time applications, and data streaming.

topics.title: NoSQL Databases
topics.description: NoSQL databases store data in formats other than traditional relational tables, such as documents, key-value pairs, graphs, or wide columns. Examples include MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, and DynamoDB. They are often chosen for use cases that require high write throughput, flexible schemas, or horizontal scalability across distributed systems.

topics.title: Observability
topics.description: Observability in software systems refers to the ability to understand the internal state of a system based on its external outputs, through logging, metrics, and distributed tracing. For AI-powered systems, observability also involves monitoring model outputs, tracking prompt and response quality, and detecting unexpected behavior in production.
resources: LLM Observability Explained: Why do you need LLM Observability?

topics.title: OpenClaw
topics.description: OpenClaw is an AI-assisted development tool designed to automate the integration and interaction between complex software systems and large language models. It functions by providing a structured framework for developers to execute code generation, refactoring, and debugging tasks directly within their existing environment, effectively lowering the barrier for rapid prototyping.
resources: OpenClaw Tutorial for Beginners - Crash Course

topics.title: OpenCode
topics.description: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that runs in the terminal. It works with many model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and locally hosted models, so you are not tied to a single vendor. It can read and edit files across a project, run shell commands and work through multi-step tasks. FDEs often work in customer environments with strict rules about which models and data can be used. A provider-agnostic, open-source tool lets them keep the same workflow when a customer approves only one provider, or requires a self-hosted model.
resources: OpenCode Tutorial for Beginners: Learn 90% Of OpenCode in Under 25 Minutes

topics.title: PostgreSQL
topics.description: PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source relational database system that supports advanced features like JSONB storage, full-text search, window functions, and custom data types. It goes well beyond what basic SQL databases offer and is a widely used default in both startups and large organizations.
resources: Learn PostgreSQL Tutorial - Full Course for Beginners

topics.title: Presenting Options
topics.description: When a major technical decision needs stakeholder buy-in, the goal is to lay out the options, explain the tradeoffs of each, and make a clear recommendation. The presentation should be structured around what matters most to the audience, not around technical completeness.

topics.title: Product Feedback Loop
topics.description: A product feedback loop is the cycle of shipping something, collecting feedback from users or stakeholders, and using that input to improve future iterations. This usually means working closely with the customer to observe how the delivered product is actually being used, identifying gaps between expectation and reality, and feeding those observations back into the build process while still on the engagement.
resources: Open the AI Product Builder roadmap
What is a product feedback loop (and how do I implement it)?
Product Feedback Loop: Definition, 5 Steps, Types & Examples (2026)

topics.title: Productized Consulting
topics.description: Productized consulting refers to a model where a consulting engagement delivers not just advice or a custom solution but a repeatable, packaged system that can be redeployed with other customers. It means building in a way that abstracts customer-specific details so the core architecture can be reused across similar engagements.
resources: How to productize consulting services: A strategic guide
Consultant’s Guide to Productization: How To Productize Consulting Services
How To Productize Your Consulting Services

topics.title: Prompt Engineering
topics.description: Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting inputs to language models in a way that produces more accurate, useful, or reliable outputs. Techniques include zero-shot and few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought reasoning, role assignment, and structured output formatting. Good prompt engineering can significantly improve model behavior without any model fine-tuning.

topics.title: Prompt Management
topics.description: Prompt management is the systematic process of creating, versioning, testing, and refining the text inputs used to guide large language models toward desired outputs. It involves maintaining a structured library of effective prompt templates, tracking how specific changes in phrasing impact model performance, and integrating these prompts into the application development lifecycle. By treating prompts as code, engineers can ensure consistency across different model versions, optimize for latency and cost, and provide a reliable interface for interacting with generative AI systems.
resources: What is prompt management? Versioning, collaboration, and deployment for prompts
Prompt Management 101 - Full Guide for AI Engineers

topics.title: Python
topics.description: Python is a general-purpose programming language known for its readable syntax and broad ecosystem. It is widely used in web development, data engineering, scripting, automation, and AI/ML workloads. Its large standard library and active package ecosystem make it practical for everything from quick scripts to large production systems.
resources: Tutorial Series: How to Code in Python

topics.title: RAGs
topics.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a pattern where relevant documents or data are fetched from a knowledge source and injected into a model's context before generating a response. This gives the model access to specific or up-to-date information without requiring fine-tuning. RAG systems typically combine a retrieval step (using embeddings or search) with a generation step (using an LLM).
resources: RAG Explained: Understanding Embeddings, Similarity, and Retrieval

topics.title: React
topics.description: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces using a component-based model. Each component manages its own state and rendering logic, and components are composed to build complete interfaces. It is one of the most widely used frontend frameworks in production web applications.
resources: React Tutorial Full Course - Beginner to Pro

topics.title: Requirements Gathering
topics.description: Project requirements come from observation as much as from conversation. You watch how teams actually work, not just how they describe their work, because those two things are often different. The goal is to surface the undocumented workflow, the data source people actually trust, and the edge cases that would break an agent in its first week of production. Written requirements are useful, but the real requirements live in the room with the people doing the work.
resources: Requirement Gathering Techniques For A Business Analyst

topics.title: ROI & AI Impact
topics.description: Understanding return on investment (ROI) for AI projects means being able to quantify how an AI system creates value, whether through cost savings, productivity improvements, revenue growth, or risk reduction. It also means being honest about what AI can realistically deliver. FDEs who can frame AI work in business terms help customers build confidence in the investment and avoid overselling what the technology can do.
resources: How to maximize AI ROI in 2026
What is ROI and How to Calculate Return on Investment
Forward Deployed Engineering: The Complete Guide for Industrial Companies

topics.title: Roles & Responsibilities
topics.description: The FDE job has three phases: audit, evals, and deployment. In the audit phase, you embed with different teams inside the customer's organization, map their workflows, identify bottlenecks, and decide where AI can create real value and where it cannot. In the evals phase, you build systems to measure whether the AI is actually working, not just whether it produces an answer, but whether it reasons through problems the way a skilled human would. In the deployment phase, you ship the system into production, starting with the smallest possible unit of autonomy and layering on capabilities only after each step is proven to work.
resources: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) : What Is It, Skills and Scope
Forward Deployed Engineer: The Complete 2026 Report- Origin, Demand, Roles, Salary & More
This Is How Forward Deployed Engineering Is Actually Done

topics.title: Rust
topics.description: Rust is a systems programming language that focuses on safety, speed, and concurrency. It manages memory through a unique ownership model with strict compiler checks, which allows developers to prevent common bugs like null pointer dereferences and buffer overflows without needing a garbage collector. It offers high-level abstractions with the performance of low-level languages like C++, enabling the creation of efficient and reliable software for performance-critical applications.
resources: Rust Crash Course Tutorial for Beginners

topics.title: Tradeoffs: Scope, Speed, Quality
topics.description: Every project involves tradeoffs between scope (how much is built), speed (how fast it is delivered), and quality (how well it holds up over time). Reducing scope can speed things up without sacrificing quality. Cutting corners on quality can speed things up in the short term but creates problems later. FDEs need to understand and communicate these tradeoffs clearly, helping customers make informed decisions rather than just agreeing to everything and delivering less than expected.
resources: Project management triangle: Triple constraint guide
What is the Iron Triangle? Time, Cost, Quality, Scope?

topics.title: Technical Scoping & Sequencing
topics.description: Technical scoping involves breaking a project into discrete tasks, estimating their complexity, and identifying dependencies. Sequencing means ordering those tasks logically, starting with the highest-risk or most uncertain parts. A well-scoped and sequenced project is easier to track and deliver on time, and gives the customer visibility into what is being built and in what order.
resources: How to effectively scope your software projects
The Ultimate Guide to Scoping Consulting Projects: A Step-by-Step Framework
Sequence Activities to Improve Project Scheduling

topics.title: Security
topics.description: Security in software systems means protecting applications, data, and infrastructure from unauthorized access, misuse, or attack. For AI systems, there are additional concerns like prompt injection, model abuse, and unintended data leakage through model outputs.
resources: What Is LLM (Large Language Model) Security? | Starter Guide
OWASP's Top 10 Ways to Attack LLMs: AI Vulnerabilities Exposed

topics.title: Spark
topics.description: Apache Spark is a distributed computing framework for processing large datasets in parallel across a cluster. It supports batch processing, streaming, SQL queries, and machine learning through a unified API. It is widely used in data engineering workflows where data volumes exceed what can be processed on a single machine.
resources: PySpark - Zero to Hero | PySpark Tutorial

topics.title: SQL
topics.description: SQL, or Structured Query Language, is the standard language for interacting with relational databases. It is used to create, read, update, and delete records, and to define the structure of tables and their relationships. Knowing SQL well is foundational for any work involving relational data storage.

topics.title: Stakeholder Management
topics.description: Stakeholder management in FDE work is less about keeping people happy and more about making sure the right people know what is happening before it becomes a problem. This means identifying who the skeptics are early, giving them the evidence they need to trust the system (usually evals), managing expectations before a demo rather than after it goes wrong, and escalating blockers fast rather than letting them quietly slow the engagement. The technical work can be excellent, and the engagement can still fail if the people who need to approve, adopt, or fund the system never get bought in.
resources: Stakeholder Management Guide: Definitions, Processes & More
Your Ultimate Guide to Effective Stakeholder Management
What is Stakeholder Management? Project Management in Under 5

topics.title: System of Record
topics.description: A system of record is the authoritative source of truth for a particular type of data within an organization. For customer data it might be Salesforce. For financial data it might be SAP. For HR data it might be Workday. Identifying the system of record early in an engagement matters because any system that touches that data needs to integrate with it correctly, not with a copy or a cache that may be stale.

topics.title: Technical Writing
topics.description: Technical writing is the practice of producing clear, accurate, and useful documentation for software systems. This includes API docs, architecture decision records, runbooks, onboarding guides, and design documents. Technical writing is especially important because good documentation is often what allows a customer to operate and extend a system after the engagement ends, without needing to call the FDE back for every question.
resources: What Is Technical Writing? A Comprehensive Guide

topics.title: Terraform
topics.description: Terraform is an open-source infrastructure-as-code tool by HashiCorp that lets engineers define cloud resources in configuration files and provision or update them automatically. It works across multiple cloud providers and is the standard tool for managing infrastructure in a repeatable, version-controlled way.
resources: Complete Terraform Course - From BEGINNER to PRO! (Learn Infrastructure as Code)

topics.title: Time-to-Value
topics.description: Time-to-value is the elapsed time between the start of an engagement and the moment the customer has something they can actually use. Compressing it means shipping a working feature early rather than designing the perfect system, prioritizing the work that demonstrates the most value first, and sequencing deliverables so that trust builds incrementally. An engagement that produces something useful in week one and keeps improving is almost always better received than one that produces something polished in week six.
resources: What Is TTV: A Complete Guide to Time to Value
What Is Time to Value (TTV) — And How Do You Measure It?

topics.title: Tools & Functions
topics.description: Tools and functions are the mechanisms through which AI agents interact with the outside world. A tool might query a database, call an external API, run a code interpreter, or search the web. In practice, tools are defined as schemas that the model can invoke, and the application handles executing the actual function and returning the result back to the model.
resources: AI Agents Explained in Simple Terms for Beginners
What is Tool Calling? Connecting LLMs to Your Data

topics.title: UAT
topics.description: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is the process by which a customer's own team validates that a system works correctly before it goes into production. It typically involves preparing test scripts, defining acceptance criteria, and supporting the customer during testing. Passing UAT is usually the formal gate before a system is considered delivered, and it is often where last-minute scope issues surface.
resources: User Acceptance Testing (UAT): Definition, Types & Best Practices

topics.title: Vector DBs
topics.description: Vector databases store high-dimensional vector embeddings and support efficient similarity search, usually using approximate nearest neighbor algorithms. They are a core component of RAG systems and semantic search applications, where the goal is to find content semantically similar to a query rather than matching keywords.
resources: What is a Vector Database? Powering Semantic Search & AI Applications
Production RAG with LangChain & Vector Databases – Full Course

topics.title: Vibe Coding
topics.description: Vibe coding refers to using AI-assisted tools to write, edit, and iterate on code through natural language interaction, at a higher level of abstraction than traditional coding. Instead of writing every line manually, the developer describes intent and guides the AI to produce working code, reviewing and refining the output. It is a workflow shift made possible by capable code-generation models.
resources: What Is Vibe Coding? Building Software with Agentic AI

topics.title: Working with Legacy Systems
topics.description: Legacy systems are the established, often undocumented infrastructure that most large organizations run their core operations on. They may be on-prem databases with no API, ERP systems that took years and millions of dollars to migrate to, or internal tools written a decade ago that no one fully understands anymore. The approach is to build around them: wrapping them with APIs, querying them safely, and connecting them to modern infrastructure without replacing the parts the business depends on.
resources: Working With Legacy Systems: A Forward Deployed Engineer’s Survival Guide
Legacy system modernisation: challenges and common approaches
What Is Legacy Code? How AI Is Modernizing Legacy Systems
